advances: The Regime A Alternative 1 inequalities do not admit a universal monotone replacement of the variable endpoint cells by the calibrated table while retaining the actual middle-cap areas and the strict low-mass inequalities. An exact rational cell vector with the same global parameters as the calibration already disproves that replacement. The exact area-only region left for a uniform geometric argument is also derived.
author: mp_r132_regime_a_extremal_reduction
proof:
The cell identities are
\[
p+x_i+x_\ell+\zeta=1,\qquad
q+b_i+b_\ell+\omega=r.
\tag{8}
\]
The two endpoint low marginals are
\[
m_i=x_i+\zeta+b_i+\omega,\qquad
m_\ell=x_\ell+\zeta+b_\ell+\omega.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(f_i+f_\ell+f_j=-1\), the three middle caps cover the middle body, and hence
\[
c_i+c_\ell\ge s-c_j.
\tag{10}
\]
The strict low-mass inequalities say
\[
c_i<m_i^{\,\mathrm{up}}:=t-m_i,\qquad
c_\ell<m_\ell^{\,\mathrm{up}}:=t-m_\ell.
\tag{11}
\]
Adding (10)-(11) gives
\[
m_i+m_\ell<2t-s+c_j=\delta.
\tag{12}
\]
Conversely, under Regime A, accepted fact `879a3c45b5f50670` gives \(\delta<1/3<t<s\). If (12) holds, both upper bounds in (11) are positive and their sum is strictly larger than \(s-c_j\). Therefore one can choose
\[
\max\{0,s-c_j-m_\ell^{\,\mathrm{up}}\}
<c_i<
\min\{m_i^{\,\mathrm{up}},s-c_j\}
\]
when \(s-c_j>0\), and then put \(c_\ell=s-c_j-c_i\); when \(s-c_j=0\), take \(c_i=c_\ell=0\). Thus (12) is also sufficient for scalar cap values satisfying (10)-(11). By (8)-(9),
\[
m_i+m_\ell
=1+r-p-q+\zeta+\omega,
\]
so (12) is exactly (1).

The common-plane inclusion in `879a3c45b5f50670` identifies
\[
\frac{P+Q}{2}
\subseteq K\cap\{f_j\le0\}.
\]
Planar Brunn--Minkowski therefore gives the last inequality in (2). The other conditions in (2) are precisely (8), nonnegativity, and \(q>0\). This proves the asserted exact scalar projection.

Using \(p,q>0\) and the last two inequalities in (2) gives
\[
4c_j
\ge(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2
>p+q
>1+r+\zeta+\omega-\delta.
\]
Since
\[
1+r-\delta=\frac52t-c_j,
\]
this is equivalent to the first inequality in (3). Combining it with the strict root tail \(c_j+r<t\) gives the second inequality in (3).

It remains to verify the rational counterexample. The values (4) lie in the first Regime A strip because
\[
0<\frac1{16}<\frac15,\qquad
\frac{15}{16}<\frac{47}{50}<\frac{17}{16}.
\]
They satisfy
\[
c_j+r=\frac{17}{40}<\frac{89}{200}=t,
\qquad
\delta=\frac5{16}\ge\frac1{16}=r.
\tag{13}
\]
The rows (6) have totals \(1\) and \(1/16\), and \(q=1/25>0\). They give
\[
u_i=u_\ell=\frac1{1000},\qquad
v_i=v_\ell=\frac9{800},
\]
so for both \(h=i,\ell\),
\[
c_h+u_h+v_h
=\frac{43}{100}+\frac1{1000}+\frac9{800}
=\frac{1769}{4000}
<\frac{1780}{4000}
=t.
\tag{14}
\]
Their total low mass is
\[
\frac{49}{2000}<\frac5{16}=\delta,
\]
and (10) holds strictly because
\[
\frac{43}{100}+\frac{43}{100}+\frac{29}{80}
=\frac{489}{400}
>\frac{47}{50}=s.
\tag{15}
\]
Finally,
\[
\frac14\left(\sqrt{\frac{499}{500}}+\sqrt{\frac1{25}}\right)^2
<\frac{29}{80}.
\tag{16}
\]
Indeed, after multiplying by \(4\), (16) reduces to
\[
\frac25\sqrt{\frac{499}{500}}<\frac{103}{250},
\]
whose left side is less than \(2/5=100/250\). Thus (6) satisfies the scalar constraint supplied by the actual high-high midpoint containment and \(j\)-cap identification. Equations (13)-(16), together with \(\omega=0\), also verify all displayed Alternative 1 consequences of `879a3c45b5f50670`.

For the calibrated table, each low marginal equals
\[
\frac3{200}+\frac1{160}+\frac1{200}
=\frac{21}{800}.
\]
Keeping the actual cap values (5), as preservation of the strict inequalities requires, yields (7). Moreover, a common affine normalization cannot repair this: since both the counterexample and calibrated \(A_0\) rows have total area \(1\), its determinant must have absolute value \(1\), and then it preserves every cell area. Any non-affine replacement would require new geometric input to preserve the common-plane midpoint inclusion and the identity of the middle caps. Such input is absent from the Regime A inequalities. This proves the claimed refutation and leaves precisely the variable scalar region (2) for a parameter-uniform geometric argument.
statement:
Use the Alternative 1 notation of accepted fact `879a3c45b5f50670`, and write the two closed cell rows as
\[
(p,x_i,x_\ell,\zeta)
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
(q,b_i,b_\ell,\omega),
\]
where
\[
x_i=u_i-\zeta,\quad x_\ell=u_\ell-\zeta,\quad
b_i=v_i-\omega,\quad b_\ell=v_\ell-\omega.
\]
The exact projection of the strict low-mass inequalities and the middle-cap covering inequality onto the cell variables is
\[
p+q>1+r+\zeta+\omega-\delta,
\qquad
\delta=2t-s+c_j.
\tag{1}
\]
After also retaining the scalar consequence of common-plane midpoint containment and identification of the high-high midpoint body with the \(j\)-cap, the surviving area-only region is exactly
\[
\begin{gathered}
p>0,\quad q>0,\quad \zeta,\omega\ge0,\quad
p+\zeta\le1,\quad q+\omega\le r,\\
p+q>1+r+\zeta+\omega-\delta,\qquad
\frac14(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2\le c_j,
\tag{2}\\
x_i+x_\ell=1-p-\zeta,\qquad
b_i+b_\ell=r-q-\omega,
\end{gathered}
\]
with arbitrary nonnegative splits in the last line. Here “exact” refers to the projection of the listed scalar area inequalities, not to polygonal realizability of every point of (2). In particular, (2) sharpens the accepted scalar consequence to
\[
c_j>\frac t2+\frac{\zeta+\omega}{5},
\qquad
8r+\frac95(\zeta+\omega)<1+s.
\tag{3}
\]

At the same global parameters as the calibration in accepted fact `bc026780453747b8`, namely
\[
r=\frac1{16},\quad s=\frac{47}{50},\quad
t=\frac{89}{200},\quad c_j=\frac{29}{80},\quad
\delta=\frac5{16},
\tag{4}
\]
take
\[
c_i=c_\ell=\frac{43}{100}
\tag{5}
\]
and the exact variable cell rows
\[
\boxed{
\left(\frac{499}{500},\frac1{1000},\frac1{1000},0\right),
\qquad
\left(\frac1{25},\frac9{800},\frac9{800},0\right).
}
\tag{6}
\]
This is feasible for every Regime A Alternative 1 scalar inequality, including the strict low-mass inequalities, the root tail, cap covering, and the high-high midpoint-cap area constraint. However, replacing (6) by the calibrated rows of `bc026780453747b8` while retaining (4)-(5) changes each low marginal from \(49/4000\) to \(21/800\), and gives
\[
\frac{43}{100}+\frac{21}{800}
=\frac{365}{800}
>\frac{356}{800}
=t.
\tag{7}
\]
Thus the required strict low-mass inequalities are destroyed. Hence the proposed universal monotone extremal reduction is false. A proof for all actual Alternative 1 instances must use variable-cell geometry on the full region (2), rather than substitute the calibrated table.
